questions.question: Explain Lokadharmi and Natyadharmi. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain Lokadharmi and Natyadharmi. [U] / [CO1]
  • • Lokadharmi refers to realistic representation of life
  • • Natyadharmi represents stylized theatrical performance mode
  • • Lokadharmi imitates everyday human behaviour naturally
  • • Natyadharmi uses gestures, mudras, and symbolism
  • • Both concepts derived from Natya Shastra tradition
  • • Used in classical Indian theatre like Kathakali
  • • They complement each other in stage presentation

questions.question: Evaluate the symbolic and narrative qualities of Romanesque church art. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the symbolic and narrative qualities of Romanesque church art. [A] / [CO2]
  • • Extensive use of symbolic religious imagery and figures
  • • Narrative relief sculptures depict Biblical events clearly
  • • Art served didactic purpose for common people
  • • Human figures appear stylized and less naturalistic
  • • Frescoes and mosaics decorate interior church spaces
  • • Portal sculptures guide believers entering church space
  • • Emphasis on spiritual message over visual realism
  • • Strong storytelling through sequential visual panels
  • • Limited perspective and anatomical accuracy in figures
  • • Reinforced Christian teachings and doctrines visually
  • • Example: Tympanum sculptures in Romanesque churches

questions.question: Critically analyze Abstract Art as a break from traditional representation. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Critically analyze Abstract Art as a break from traditional representation. [An] / [CO3]
  • • Rejects realistic depiction of physical objects completely
  • • Focuses on colour, line, and abstract forms
  • • Expresses emotions directly without representational imagery
  • • Breaks rules of perspective and natural proportion
  • • Encourages subjective interpretation by individual viewers
  • • Developed as part of modernist artistic movements
  • • Artists experiment with materials and techniques freely
  • • Non-objective art removes dependence on real-world subjects
  • • Challenges conventional definition and purpose of art
  • • Influenced later contemporary and conceptual art forms
  • • Example: Kandinsky’s abstract compositions
